blindSummary:
This state/province holds the most trans-visible public space in the country: a centuries-old trans-feminine monastic order paraded at the country's biggest religious festival — the world's largest religious gathering — with one of its highest-ranking ascetics leading ceremonial bathing (Jan–Feb 2025), so a trans visitor at that festival is inside an institutionally recognised religious hierarchy, not a marginalised underground. This state/province also has a constituted transgender welfare board.

Situated modestly above the country-wide average. The monastic order's inclusion is visitor-facing, seasonal, and institutionally validated by the council of orders' wider governance structures. A counterweight exists — one transgender woman was strangled during a robbery in a large industrial city (Aug 2025) — but this is a lone incident with no patterned state-actor response and does not constitute a regional finding under the single-incident rule. Against some larger peer states, this state/province lacks a comprehensive transgender policy framework or judicial endorsement; against another peer state, it does not show the festival-entry religion-screening that creates outing mechanisms at public gatherings. The net positive is narrow and temporally concentrated.
